use serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};

use crate::ids::{ObjectId, PlayerId};
use crate::types::{Zone, Step, ManaType};
use crate::state::GameResult;

/// Events emitted by state transitions. Used for game log, triggered abilities (future),
/// and UI updates.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum GameEvent {
    GameStarted,
    TurnStarted { player: PlayerId, turn: u32 },
    StepStarted { step: Step },
    CardDrawn { player: PlayerId, object: ObjectId },
    LandPlayed { player: PlayerId, object: ObjectId },
    SpellCast { player: PlayerId, object: ObjectId },
    SpellResolved { object: ObjectId },
    ManaAdded { player: PlayerId, mana_type: ManaType, amount: u32 },
    ManaPoolEmptied { player: PlayerId },
    EnteredBattlefield { object: ObjectId, controller: PlayerId },
    LeftBattlefield { object: ObjectId, to: Zone },
    ObjectMoved { object: ObjectId, from: Zone, to: Zone },
    Tapped { object: ObjectId },
    Untapped { object: ObjectId },
    AttackersDeclared { attackers: Vec<(ObjectId, PlayerId)> },
    BlockersDeclared { assignments: Vec<(ObjectId, ObjectId)> },
    CombatDamageDealt { source: ObjectId, target: DamageTarget, amount: u32 },
    /// Non-combat damage dealt (e.g., triggered abilities, spells).
    NonCombatDamageDealt { source: ObjectId, target: DamageTarget, amount: u32 },
    LifeChanged { player: PlayerId, old: i32, new_life: i32 },
    CreatureDied { object: ObjectId, card_id: crate::ids::CardId, controller: PlayerId, damaged_by: Vec<ObjectId>, last_known_toughness: i32 },
    PlayerLost { player: PlayerId, reason: LossReason },
    GameEnded { result: GameResult },
    PriorityPassed { player: PlayerId },
    Discarded { player: PlayerId, object: ObjectId },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum DamageTarget {
    Player(PlayerId),
    Object(ObjectId),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum LossReason {
    LifeReachedZero,
    DrewFromEmptyLibrary,
    Conceded,
}

198	impl std::fmt::Display for TargetFilter {
199	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
200	        match self {
201	            TargetFilter::Any => write!(f, "any"),
202	            TargetFilter::YouControl => write!(f, "you control"),
203	            TargetFilter::YouDontControl => write!(f, "you don't control"),
204	            TargetFilter::Nonblack => write!(f, "nonblack"),
205	            TargetFilter::NotSubtypes(types) => write!(f, "non-{}", types.join("/")),
206	            TargetFilter::PowerAtLeast(n) => write!(f, "power {}+", n),
207	            TargetFilter::Attacking => write!(f, "attacking"),
208	            TargetFilter::Noncreature => write!(f, "noncreature"),
209	            TargetFilter::HasCardType(types) => {
210	                let names: Vec<&str> = types.iter().map(|t| match t {
211	                    CardType::Artifact => "artifact",
212	                    CardType::Enchantment => "enchantment",
213	                    CardType::Creature => "creature",
214	                    CardType::Instant => "instant",
215	                    CardType::Sorcery => "sorcery",
216	                    CardType::Land => "land",
217	                    CardType::Planeswalker => "planeswalker",
218	                }).collect();
219	                write!(f, "{}", names.join(" or "))
220	            }
221	            TargetFilter::HasSubtype(subtype) => write!(f, "{}", subtype),
222	            TargetFilter::Another => write!(f, "another"),
223	            TargetFilter::SameNameAsSource => write!(f, "with the same name"),
224	            TargetFilter::SubtypeOrCardType { subtypes, card_types } => {
225	                let mut parts: Vec<String> = subtypes.clone();
226	                for t in card_types {
227	                    parts.push(match t {
228	                        CardType::Enchantment => "enchantment".into(),
229	                        CardType::Artifact => "artifact".into(),
230	                        _ => format!("{:?}", t).to_lowercase(),
231	                    });
232	                }
233	                write!(f, "{}", parts.join(" or "))
234	            }
235	        }
236	    }

  - Official ruling says: `If Unruly Mob and another creature you control die simultaneously (perhaps because they were both attacking or blocking), Unruly Mob won't be on the battlefield as its triggered ability resolves. - "you control" constraint (opponent's creature death must not trigger Unruly Mob): PASS — `on_any_creature_dies` checks `dead_controller == controller` where `controller` is Unruly Mob's current controller; opponent-controlled creature deaths don't add a counter.

**Type line**: Creature — Human

In the code, `collect_triggers` (`triggers.rs` lines 418–419) scans for DeathWatch watchers using `filter(|o| o.zone == Zone::Battlefield && o.id != dead_id)`. When a board state has Unruly Mob and another creature with lethal damage, the SBA loop calls `destroy()` for both in sequence before `collect_triggers` is ever called. `destroy()` calls `move_object(Zone::Graveyard)` immediately. So by the time `collect_triggers` processes the other creature's `CreatureDied` event, Unruly Mob is already in the graveyard and fails the `zone == Zone::Battlefield` filter. Its trigger is never collected and never placed on the stack.

The practical game-state outcome (no counter placed) is identical to rules-correct behavior, but the trigger should appear on the stack. No test covers the simultaneous death case.
